## Purpose

Use this page for optional additions when you have extra time, a more advanced cohort, or a strong local data example to work with.

The learner [Additional Material](../learners/additional_material.qmd) provides a complete fictional dataset, source notes, four five-minute tasks, and worked answers. Start there when you need a prepared example or access fallback. The options below extend that practice; they are not extra compulsory sessions.

| Lesson | Prepared resource | Useful output |
|---|---|---|
| [Collecting the Right Data](../episodes/01-collecting_the_right_data.qmd) | Learner Task 1 or the source cards in [Extra Exercises](extra_exercises.qmd) | A collection question, population, variable list, and source limitation |
| [Organising and Exploring Data](../episodes/02-organising_and_exploring_data.qmd) | Learner Task 2 and the [practice CSV](../learners/data/practice_requests.csv) | A working copy and justified change log |
| [Making Sense of Data](../episodes/03-making_sense_of_data.qmd) | Learner Task 3 and the [chart guidance](https://analysisfunction.civilservice.gov.uk/policy-store/data-visualisation-charts/) | A checked summary and an accurate caption |
| [Insight to Impact](../episodes/04-insight_to_impacts.qmd) | Learner Task 4 | Separate evidence, interpretation, action, and evaluation statements |

## Optional Extensions

### Data Source Comparison

- Compare institutional data, survey data, open data, and manually collected data for the same question.
- Ask learners to identify what each source can and cannot justify.

### Data Cleaning Demonstration

- Show a before-and-after spreadsheet with inconsistent labels, missing values, and duplicated records.
- Ask learners which transformations should be documented.
- Use the fictional request source notes to justify each change. Compare summaries with and without the valid 50-minute response to show why removing an unusual value needs evidence.

### Visualisation Critique

- Use a gallery of charts with truncated axes, overloaded colour, missing labels, or weak context.
- Ask learners to rewrite the chart title as a claim and then test whether the chart supports it.
- Provide the underlying values, units, and source context alongside the chart. Ask for a text description that communicates the evidence without relying on colour.

### Insight Communication

- Give learners one finding and three audiences.
- Ask them to adapt the emphasis without changing the evidence.
- Compare messages for a researcher, service owner, and service user. Retain the same count, period, missingness, and uncertainty in all three.

## External Teaching Resources

The learner resource page links to verified [Data Carpentry spreadsheet lessons](https://datacarpentry.github.io/spreadsheet-ecology-lesson/), [NIST exploratory analysis guidance](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/eda.htm), and [Government Analysis Function chart guidance](https://analysisfunction.civilservice.gov.uk/policy-store/data-visualisation-charts/). Select a specific example for the cohort and check its reuse conditions before reproducing external materials.
